author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form prefilled with its current values. A correction follows booking's validation, changes that visit in place without adding another, and returns to the owner's record. The form is reached by its address alone; no page links to it.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a description and a future date are submitted, then that visit carries them, the pet gains no additional visit, and the owner's record is shown.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps its booked details.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps its booked details.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 3: correcting a visit is refused when the visit does not exist, or when it belongs to a pet other than the one named.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 4: a visit whose date has already passed is corrected only by moving its date later than today; resubmitting its past date is refused.
non_goals: A link or other visible entry point to the correction form from the owner's record or any other page (owner decision, intake line 1).
Moving a visit to a different pet: a correction changes only the date and description.
New user-facing wording for the correction, such as a confirmation message or correction-specific form labels (recorded open question).
Correcting a past-dated visit while keeping its past date (recorded open question).
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records on the log. Narrowest-reading decisions taken here, all reversible: (1) edge case 3 refuses a visit that is not the named pet's, or does not exist, mirroring booking's edge case 1; (2) the slice adds no user-facing wording, so no new text needs translating under REQ-LANG-002; (3) only date and description change. Three open questions are recorded under PRD Open Questions: entry point, past-dated visits, correction wording. The intake request (line 1) also states owner mechanism constraints (the path, reuse of the existing visit form and its model attribute); they are the design stage's to honor and are not restated in the PRD. This dispatch wrote docs/prd.md, docs/adr/2026-09-13-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md (new), and the status line of docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. The ADR index docs/adr/README.md needs a row for the new ADR; it lies outside this agent's write scope, so system-design-expert should add it and list it in its design-block.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction fits the owner aggregate as system-design.md § Overview and § Contracts (Invariants) record it: resolve through OwnerRepository.findById -> Owner.getPet -> the pet's visit, mutate the framework-mapped Visit (architecture-principles § Scoped exception), persist by saving the Owner (OwnerRepository is the sole write path; Visit persists only by cascade). Two small adjustments, both following adjacent seams: (1) VisitController's model-attribute method gains an optional visitId path variable, the create/edit switch PetController.findPet already demonstrates; with it present it resolves the existing visit and attaches nothing, without it it keeps today's new-visit path. (2) Pet gains a lookup of one of its visits by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). The template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm needs no change: its form carries no action (posts back to the edit URL), its heading drops 'New' when the visit is persisted, and the submit label is the reused booking wording the PRD records as an open question. Basis: IDE oracle not connected; covering symbols confirmed by grep and read (weaker basis) at PetController.java:75-87, Owner.java:126, VisitController.java (loadPetWithVisit, processNewVisitForm).
integration_points: Entry points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController, rendering pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with the existing 'visit' model attribute (owner mechanism constraints, intake line 1). Success redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with no flash message (PRD non-goal: no new wording); failure re-renders the form.

Binding target (correction POST): the persisted Visit resolved through owner -> pet -> visit, behind an allow-list of date and description. Realize it in VisitController's controller-wide @InitBinder: setAllowedFields for date and description, keeping the existing setDisallowedFields for id and *.id. Controller-wide, so the owner model attribute a handler takes binds nothing on booking or correction (security-principles § Realization, Mass assignment row; system-design § Threat Model mass-assignment row). The Visit is never bound whole.

Repository double: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in VisitControllerTests, a framework stub kept as a conscious exception (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Reason: OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, so a hand-written double must implement the whole inherited surface, and the prd-entry places the tests in that @WebMvcTest class. Stub only findById, returning a real Owner -> Pet -> Visit graph built from real entities with ids set; mock no domain object.

Test assertions against that double: a correction asserts the corrected date and description, and the unchanged visit count, on the Owner passed to save. A refusal asserts save is never invoked, not the in-memory visit: binding mutates the loaded (detached) graph before validation, and only save writes (system-design § Persistence, open-in-view disabled).
Transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Refusal for a missing visit or another pet's visit (edge case 3): the pet's visit lookup returns nothing and the model-attribute method throws IllegalArgumentException, mirroring booking's missing-pet refusal in the same method. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles § Realization, secret-disclosure row). Under MockMvc the unhandled exception surfaces from perform(); assert it and that save is never invoked.

patterns.description: findPet takes @PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false): one model-attribute method switches between a new instance and the resolved persisted one. loadPetWithVisit takes visitId the same way.
getPet(Integer) resolves a child by identity, skipping unsaved children, returning null when absent. Pet's visit lookup mirrors it.

processNewVisitForm's non-future-date check (rejectValue on date with typeMismatch.visitDate). Both handlers call one copy of it; the edge-case-4 refusal of a past visit's own date falls out of the same check.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit attaches a new Visit to the pet on every request. On the correction path the Owner save would cascade-insert that extra visit, breaking 'the pet gains no additional visit'.
risks.mitigation: Attach a new Visit only when visitId is absent. The success test asserts the saved pet still has exactly one visit, carrying the corrected values (system-design § Contracts, Invariants: Visit persists only by cascade from Owner).

risks.risk: Placing the date rule at the correction handler reads as a new business rule in a controller.
risks.mitigation: State the existing check once, in one private method both handlers call; no second copy, no new rule (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, the 'Controllers carry rules today' paragraph; system-design § Contracts VisitController row). Do not move it to a Form validator or a @Future constraint in this slice: where controller rules move is system-design Open Question 2, and an entity constraint would also fire at persistence.

risks.risk: Booking's handler takes the owner as a bound model attribute, so request fields matching owner properties bind onto the loaded owner and its save persists them. A correction handler copied from booking inherits this.
risks.mitigation: The controller-wide allow-list (integration points) closes it on both routes; a test may post an owner field on the correction and assert the saved owner is unchanged (security-principles § Realization, Mass assignment row: the safe state is the default, not remembered per endpoint).

notes: Design-doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md: REQ-VIS-003 joins the Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController Contracts rows, and the Pet and VisitController purposes now state the lookup and the correction. Security Context inputs name visit identifiers. The Threat Model mass-assignment row states the visit binder allow-list and the pet-scoped visit lookup. The unvalidated-input row states the date check covers correction. docs/adr/README.md: index row for the 2026-09-13 non-goal ADR, and the 2026-08-08 row's status notes the NG-5 narrowing (requested by the prd-entry notes). No ADR: the allow-list and the model-attribute switch are single-slice choices following existing seams. The two non-goal ADR edits are the product expert's, covered by the prd-entry's scope_overrides. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records on the log. Baseline, not a slice risk: saving merges the whole detached owner graph with no version column, so concurrent writes are last-write-wins, the same as booking. On a refused correction the form's previous-visits table shows the rejected values for that visit until reload; persisted state is untouched.

approved_aspects: Ownership chain re-resolved on every request (security-principles 'Trusting cross-request state' row): VisitController.java loadPetWithVisit resolves owner by path id, then 'Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);', then 'Visit visit = pet.getVisit(visitId);' with a refusal when null; Pet.java getVisit iterates only 'getVisits()' and skips 'visit.isNew()', so another pet's or owner's visit id cannot be edited through a mismatched path. Covered by VisitControllerTests.java:236 'theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitThatIsNotThePetsVisit' (another pet's visit and a missing id, asserting no save).

Mass assignment tightened rather than widened: @InitBinder now adds 'dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");' alongside the retained 'setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")', and applies to every binder in the controller, including the loaded Owner bound via '@ModelAttribute Owner owner'. This closes owner-field binding (e.g. address) through both the new correction POST and the existing booking POST; Visit.java binds only 'date' and 'description' (fields read at Visit.java:40 and :43). Verified by VisitControllerTests.java:248 'theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveTheOwnersDetailsUnchanged' posting an address param.

Validation holds on the new persisting path: processVisitCorrectionForm takes '@Valid Visit visit' and calls the shared rejectNonFutureDate before 'this.owners.save(owner)'; the booking path's date check was extracted into the same helper, not weakened.

No new injection or XSS sink: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders description with 'th:text' (no th:utext; grep of the diff for utext/Runtime/ProcessBuilder/logger/System.out returned no production hits); the form has no action attribute, so the edit form posts back to its own edit URL. Data access stays on OwnerRepository.findById/save; no query text composed.

New exception message carries only integer path ids ('Visit with id ' + visitId + ' not found for pet with id ' + petId ...), consistent with the existing owner/pet not-found messages; error.html:18 renders ${message} but nothing sensitive reaches it. visitId is an Integer path variable, so no free text enters the message.

No secrets added: grep of the full changeset diff for password|secret|token|apikey|credential matched only a system-design.md docs line describing existing env-var credentials. No dependency change (build.gradle absent from 'scripts/changeset.sh --name-only'). No NVD match ran: dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (grep of build.gradle for dependencyCheck|owasp: no hit); resolved runtime versions from './gradlew dependencies': spring-boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE.

New endpoint surface stated: GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit are open like every other mutating route, which is the recorded demonstration baseline (security-principles.md line 26); system-design.md threat-model row updated to describe the visit binder allow-list and path resolution.

author: change-grader
summary: add correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Two prod files in one package (VisitController, Pet) plus their test class and scoped docs; no sensitive paths. VisitController is a declared security surface, and its binder edit reaches the existing booking route, but the reach stays inside one controller.

semantic_surprise.note: Two behaviors a 'visit correction' diff would not lead a reader to expect. First, the one-line controller-wide setAllowedFields("date", "description") at VisitController.java:58 also changes the existing booking POST, which no longer binds owner fields: a deliberate, design-recorded hardening, but a silent change to a route the request does not name. Second, rejectNonFutureDate skips a null date, Visit.date carries no @NotNull, and visit_date is nullable in all three schemas, so a correction posted with an empty date passes validation and saves a null date over the booked one. Booking has the same gap, but on a correction it erases existing data.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real. They drive MockMvc against real Owner, Pet, and Visit graphs, assert the corrected values and the unchanged visit count by recursive comparison, assert that save is never called on each refusal (blank, today, past, a past visit keeping its date, another pet's visit, a missing visit), and pin the owner-field binding block. Gaps: no empty-date correction case, and no booking-route test for the allow-list (the shared line is still exercised through the correction test).

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved. The final roster was code-quality-reviewer alone, re-reviewing a fix delta that touched only Javadoc and resolved its two autofix findings. The doc-reviewer's single recommendation is a sentence-length nit on a PRD bullet, made in round one. The cited lines I spot-checked resolve (VisitControllerTests.java:236 and :248, Owner.java:126). No reviewer raised the empty-date path.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The changed files match the prd-entry file_targets. The template is untouched and no edit link was added, per the owner's decision. The booking-route binder change came from the design-block's integration points and risks, not from a fix round.

rationale: This change is correct, well tested, and cleanly approved, but two behaviors need a read. The controller-wide binder allow-list silently changes the existing booking route. A correction posted with an empty date passes validation and saves a null date over the booked one. Read VisitController.java:57-58 and rejectNonFutureDate, and decide whether the empty-date gap is acceptable, before merging.
